name: Following Directions
blurb: Listen carefully, then pick the picture that matches.
childIntro: I will say something once. Listen right to the end. Then find the picture that matches everything I said.
howItWorks: The teacher reads a description aloud, once, and the child marks the picture that fits. It appears only at OLSAT levels A, B and C, which are kindergarten through second grade, because it is a listening task that cannot exist once children read for themselves. The difficulty comes from position words like between, above and next to, and from having to satisfy every condition at once.
parentTip: This is the question type you can practice anywhere, with no materials. In the car, say: point to something red that is smaller than your hand. Build up to two and then three conditions. The skill is holding all of them in mind while checking, which is exactly what the test measures. Remember the real test says it once with no repeats.

questions.prompt: Point to the picture with the cat in the middle.
questions.explanation: In the middle means with one thing on each side. Only choice a has the cat between the two trees.
questions.strategy: Middle means one thing on the left and one on the right.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a bird above a flower.

figure.alt: A stack of pictures, top to bottom.
A stack of pictures, top to bottom.
A stack of pictures, top to bottom.
A stack of pictures, top to bottom.

questions.explanation: Above means higher up. The bird has to be on top and the flower underneath. Choice b has them the wrong way round.
questions.strategy: Above means on top. Below means underneath.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a star above a moon.

figure.alt: A star with a moon underneath it
A moon with a star underneath it
Two stars
Two moons

questions.explanation: Above means higher up. The star has to be on top and the moon underneath. Choice b has them the wrong way round.
questions.strategy: Above means on top. Below means underneath. They are opposites.

questions.prompt: Find the picture that shows three apples and one banana.
questions.explanation: Count both. Three apples and one banana. Choice b has the numbers swapped and choice d has no banana at all.
questions.strategy: When you hear two numbers, count both before you choose.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with two cats and one dog.
questions.explanation: Count both. Two cats and one dog. Choice b has the numbers swapped and choice d has no dog at all.
questions.strategy: When you hear two numbers, count both before you choose.

questions.prompt: Find the picture where the star is last.
questions.explanation: Last means at the end, on the right. Only choice a has the star at the end.
questions.strategy: First, second, last. Count from the left with your finger.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a dog that is NOT next to a ball.
questions.explanation: The word NOT flips it. You want the dog with no ball beside it. Choices b and c both put a ball right next to the dog. Choice d has no dog at all.
questions.strategy: The word NOT changes everything. Listen for it and then look for the opposite.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a small triangle to the right of a big square.

figure.alt: A big blue square then a small green triangle
A small green triangle then a big blue square
A big blue square then a big green triangle
A small blue square then a small green triangle

questions.explanation: Three things had to be right: the square is big, the triangle is small, and the triangle is on the right. Choice b has it on the left, choice c has the triangle too big, choice d has the square too small.
questions.strategy: Three conditions means three checks. Go through them in order.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a fish that is NOT next to a boat.
questions.explanation: The word NOT flips it. You want the fish with no boat beside it. Choices b and c both put a boat next to the fish.
questions.strategy: The word NOT changes everything. Listen for it.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with more apples than bananas.
questions.explanation: Count each fruit. Choice a has two apples and one banana, so there really are more apples. Choice c has the same number of each, which is not more.
questions.strategy: More than means bigger. The same number does not count.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a sun between two clouds.
questions.explanation: Between means in the middle with one thing on each side, and both sides must be clouds. Choice d has suns on the outside.
questions.strategy: Check the middle first, then check both sides match.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a small circle to the right of a big square.

figure.alt: A big blue square then a small red circle
A small red circle then a big blue square
A big blue square then a big red circle
A small blue square then a small red circle

questions.explanation: Three things had to be right: the square is big, the circle is small, and the circle is on the right. Choice b puts it on the left and choice c makes it too big.
questions.strategy: Three conditions means three checks. Go through them in order.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with three trees and no houses.
questions.explanation: Two things had to be true: three trees AND no houses. Choice b has a house in it and choice c has only two trees.
questions.strategy: When the sentence says AND, both parts must be true.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a cat first and a bird last.
questions.explanation: The cat must be at the front AND the bird at the end. Choice c has the cat first but the bird in the middle. Choice d has the bird last but a dog first.
questions.strategy: Two positions to check. Look at the front and the back.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with neither a car nor a bus.
questions.explanation: Neither one nor the other means both are ruled out. Choice b has a car and choice c has a bus. That leaves the bicycles.
questions.strategy: Neither and nor means say no to both. Cross them off.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with the same number of stars as moons.
questions.explanation: The same number means an equal count of each. Choice a has two of each. Every other choice has more of one than the other.
questions.strategy: Count each kind separately, then compare the two numbers.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a small shape inside a big circle.

figure.alt: A circle and a star side by side

questions.explanation: Inside means one shape drawn within the other, and the big one must be the circle. Choice b has them swapped and choice c has them side by side.
questions.strategy: Inside, outside and beside are three different places. Picture it first.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a heart inside a circle.

figure.alt: A circle and a heart side by side

questions.explanation: Inside means one shape is drawn within the other. The heart has to be the one inside. Choice b has them swapped and choice c has them side by side.
questions.strategy: Inside, outside and beside are three different places. Picture it before you look.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with more cats than dogs.
questions.explanation: Count each animal. Choice a has two cats and one dog, so there really are more cats. Choice c has the same number of each, which is not more.
questions.strategy: More than means bigger. The same number does not count.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with more books than pencils.
questions.explanation: Count each thing. Choice a has three books and one pencil, so there are more books. Choice c has the same number of each.
questions.strategy: More than means bigger. Equal does not count.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a bird that is neither in a tree nor in a nest.

choices.label: a tree and a nest, no bird

questions.explanation: Neither one nor the other means both are ruled out. Choice b is in a tree and choice c is in a nest, so both are out. Choice d has no bird. That leaves the bird in the sky.
questions.strategy: Neither and nor means say no to both. Cross them off, then see what is left.

questions.prompt: Find the picture where the second shape is a star.

figure.alt: circle, star, square
star, circle, square
circle, square, star
star, star, circle

questions.explanation: Second means the one in position number two, counting from the left. Choice b has the star first and choice c has it third.
questions.strategy: First, second, third. Count from the left with your finger.

questions.prompt: Find the picture where the second thing is a key.
questions.explanation: Second means position number two, counting from the left. Choice b has the key first and choice c has it third.
questions.strategy: First, second, third. Count from the left.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with exactly two things that are the same.

choices.label: an apple, a banana and grapes

questions.explanation: Exactly two must match and the third must be different. Choices b and d are all the same, and choice c has no matching pair.
questions.strategy: Read the sentence twice. Exactly two, and one different.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a cup that is neither on a table nor in a sink.

choices.label: a table and a sink, no cup

questions.explanation: Neither one nor the other rules out both. Choice b is on a table, choice c is in a sink, and choice d has no cup at all. That leaves the basket.
questions.strategy: Cross off both named places, then see what is left.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with exactly two shapes that are the same color, and one that is different.

figure.alt: blue, blue, green
all blue
all different
all green

questions.explanation: Two must match and one must not. Choice a has two blue and one green. Choices b and d are all the same, and choice c has no matching pair at all.
questions.strategy: Read the sentence twice in your head. Exactly two, and exactly one different.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with one more cat than dogs.
questions.explanation: One more means the cats beat the dogs by exactly one. Choice c has the same number of each and choice d has no dogs at all.
questions.strategy: One more is an exact amount, not just any bigger number.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a star on top, a moon in the middle and a sun at the bottom.

figure.alt: A stack of pictures, top to bottom.
A stack of pictures, top to bottom.
A stack of pictures, top to bottom.
A stack of pictures, top to bottom.

questions.explanation: Three positions had to be right. Every other choice has at least one in the wrong place.
questions.strategy: Build the stack in your head from the top down.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with fewer fish than boats.
questions.explanation: Fewer means a smaller number. Choice a has one fish and two boats. Choice c has the same number of each.
questions.strategy: Fewer means less. Check which side is smaller.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a red shape between two blue shapes.

figure.alt: blue, red, blue
red, blue, blue
blue, blue, red
red, blue, red

questions.explanation: Between means in the middle with one on each side, and both outer shapes must be blue. Choice d has the colors the wrong way round.
questions.strategy: Check the middle first, then check both sides match.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with three things that are all different.

choices.label: an apple, a banana and grapes

questions.explanation: Three things AND all different. Choice b has two the same, choice c has all three the same, and choice d has only two things.
questions.strategy: Two conditions: the right number, and all different.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a cat that is not first and not last.
questions.explanation: Not first and not last leaves only the middle. Choice b has the cat first and choice c has it last.
questions.strategy: When two positions are ruled out, only one is left.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with twice as many stars as moons.
questions.explanation: Twice as many means double. Four stars is double two moons. Choice b has three and one, which is three times as many, not twice.
questions.strategy: Twice as many means count the small group, then double it.

questions.prompt: Find the picture with a tree behind a house.

choices.label: a tree with a house in front
a house with a tree in front

questions.explanation: Behind means the tree is further back, so the house is the one you see in front. Choice b has them the other way round.
questions.strategy: Behind and in front are opposites. Work out which one is nearer.
